builder.policyTitle: Who answers and what is shown
builder.policySummaryOrganisation: Organisations · named answers · attributed to the company
builder.policySummaryOptional: Individuals · the respondent chooses · results from {k} answers
builder.policySummaryAnonymous: Individuals · anonymous answers · results from {k} answers
builder.policyKindNotePerson: Employees, customers, members or residents. Their answers are protected by a threshold.
builder.policyKindNoteOrganisation: Suppliers or providers answering on behalf of a company. Answers are shown with the company name.
builder.policyAnonNoteOrganisation: Fixed to «Named» — organisations always answer attributed.
builder.policyLowText: With a threshold of {k}, answers from small groups become easier to link to individuals. The results may then count as personal data, with the deletion and access rights that entails. Consider «Named» instead if you genuinely want to see who answered.
builder.policyTwoText: At a threshold of 2, whoever answers can work out what the other person answered: they know their own answer, they see the result, and they subtract. That is not weakened anonymity — it is disclosure by arithmetic. If seeing individual answers is the point, «Med navn» is the mode that does that without promising something it cannot keep. At a threshold of 2 the aggregate is also personal data in practice.
builder.policyWarnTargetBelow: The group has {target} recipients. With a threshold of {k} the result will never be shown.
builder.policyError_forbidden: Only an administrator can change this.
builder.policyError_locked: Cannot be changed now — the survey has been sent or is governed by a statutory template.
builder.policyError_belowOrgFloor: The organisation has set a floor for the threshold and this value is below it. An administrator changes the floor under Administrasjon → Personvern.
builder.lockedNotice: This survey has been sent. The questions cannot be changed now — copy it as a new round to make changes.
builder.addDescScale: One type — pick the style afterwards: numbers, words, faces, 0–10 or a slider
builder.addDescDropdown: Long lists without taking up space
builder.addDescText: Their own words — put it last
builder.logicRule: A low score on “{question}” → the respondent gets a follow-up question
builder.audNoteAnsatte: Employee mode: anonymity first. Individual prizes are not recommended — they colour the answers.
builder.audNoteKunder: Customer mode: NPS/CSAT, consent to follow-up and prizes are allowed.
builder.incIngenDesc: Curiosity and usefulness alone — safest for data quality
builder.incLotteri: A draw among everyone who answers
builder.incLotteriDesc: Drawn regardless of what you answer
builder.incAlleDesc: A discount code or coffee on the house
builder.incVeldedig: A gift to a good cause
builder.incVeldedigDesc: We donate an amount per response
builder.charityPlaceholder: Which cause — and how much per response?
builder.incentiveWarning: Prizes for employees can produce “correct” answers rather than honest ones. Consider a gift to a good cause instead.
builder.tPersonalDesc: “Hi Marit” and a named sender raise the open rate
builder.tDeadline: Show the deadline in the invitation
builder.tDeadlineDesc: A concrete date beats “as soon as possible”
builder.tRevealResultsDesc: Reciprocity — the strongest driver without a prize
builder.tFollowUpDesc: The respondent can ask to be contacted
builder.cLavDesc: Asks “what would have lifted it?” when the answer is 1–2 or no
builder.cAlleDesc: An optional field under each question
builder.cNoteLav: Recommended: conditional follow-up gives the most usable free text without making the survey longer.
builder.cNoteAlle: Comment fields everywhere give a lot of text, but often empty fields. Can be overridden per question in advanced mode.
builder.cNoteIngen: Can still be switched on for individual questions in advanced mode.
builder.expectedNote: Estimate based on the choices above and the length of the survey
builder.expectedNoteLong: Pulled down by the length — over 8 questions costs around 12 percentage points
builder.testHint: You answer as a respondent. Nothing is stored.
builder.runModeDesc: Decides which question types and settings you get.
builder.runModeNamedSurvey: Live requires anonymous answers. The QR gives each device a one-time link, and the system does not know who the device belongs to.
builder.feedbackDesc: Respondents can add a comment to each question and start a conversation. You reply without seeing who wrote it, if the comment is anonymous. Everything is collected under Actions.
builder.feedbackOffDesc: No comment field on the questions
builder.feedbackAnonymousDesc: The comment is stored without a name. You can reply, and the reply appears for the respondent in the same link she answered from.
builder.feedbackOptionalDesc: The respondent chooses anonymous or named once, and the choice applies to the whole submission
builder.feedbackLinkOnly: Surveys shared only by link or QR have no thread: the comment arrives, but there is no recipient to reply to.
builder.feedbackFailed: Could not save the setting. Try again.
builder.quizTimeBonusDesc: A faster correct answer scores more
builder.quizInstantUnavailable: Not built. All answers are shown at the end.
builder.quizCertificateUnavailable: Not built. A quiz has no pass mark.
builder.quizWillName: A quiz awards points to a person. Choosing Quiz sets the survey to «By name».
builder.quizSwitchedToNamed: The survey is now «By name» — that is what a quiz needs in order to award points.
builder.quizPackLocked: The template locks the run mode. A statutory survey has no correct answers, so it cannot become a quiz.
builder.quizNotKeyable: This question type cannot have an answer key
builder.quizAddNote: Quiz mode: multiple choice with up to four options is drawn as large coloured tiles with shapes. More than four falls back to an ordinary list.

admin.anonExplainer: Anonymous answers are never stored with a link to a user. The display threshold is {k} for new surveys and never lower than two, and free text is never shown with a group when the group is below the threshold. Nobody — not even an administrator — can look up who answered what.
admin.brandAccentNote: The figure is the contrast between dark text (#191510) and the coloured surface. Accents are used as a surface behind dark text, never as a text colour. We do not offer a free colour picker, because arbitrary colours quickly fall below the 4.5:1 requirement.
admin.brandLogoDarkSpec: Used in Live and in dark e-mail
admin.brandLogoLightSpec: SVG or PNG · min. 240 px wide
admin.brandSenderDeferred: Sender, per-template locking and default subject lines belong on this tab, but they require a sender domain verified against the e-mail provider. They are built together with sending, not here — while nothing can be verified, a status chip would be decoration.
admin.brandTooLarge: The file is too large. Maximum 2 MB.
admin.brandWrongType: That file type is not supported. Use SVG, PNG, JPG or WebP.
admin.companyNote: The organisation number and contact person are used in the data processing agreement and in the footer of the invitations respondents receive.
admin.controllerBody: {org} is the data controller for the personal data. HeiTuva is the data processor and processes data only on instruction.
admin.controllerNote: {company} is the data controller for the personal data. HeiTuva is the data processor and only processes data on instruction.
admin.directoryOverridden: Changed here — Entra ID will overwrite it on the next sync
admin.docsComing: Document upload is coming in a later phase.
admin.dsrDeadline: Deadline: 30 days after the request is received

admin.dsrPortabilitetDesc: Export in a machine-readable format (JSON or CSV)
admin.dsrRettingDesc: Correct errors in name, email or group
admin.dsrSlettingDesc: Removes all identifiable data about the person
admin.errDuplicate: That email address is already registered.
admin.errForbidden: You do not have permission to change this.

admin.errSsoLastBreakGlass: This is the last administrator who can sign in without Entra ID. Mark another one first, or turn off the Entra ID requirement.
admin.errSsoNoBreakGlass: First mark at least one active administrator under “Can sign in without Entra ID” — otherwise nobody could recover if Entra ID failed.
admin.errSsoSelf: Sign in with Entra ID yourself first, or mark yourself under “Can sign in without Entra ID” — otherwise you would be signed out on the next request.
admin.errSsoUnavailable: Entra ID is not set up for HeiTuva yet, so sign-in cannot require it.
admin.groupThresholdNote: Groups below the threshold never get their own results
admin.inviteFailed: Could not invite. Check the email address.
admin.langIntro: Change how HeiTuva reads for your organisation. Changes apply only to you, and “Reset” always brings the standard text back. Text you leave alone follows along when HeiTuva is updated.
admin.langPlaceholderMismatch: The text must use the same variables as the standard:
admin.mgBelowThreshold: Below the organisation’s threshold ({k}) — results are not shown
admin.mgCreatedSegment: The segment is created and updates itself
admin.mgDuplicate: An audience with that name already exists.
admin.mgGroupsDesc: Fixed lists. Synced groups update automatically.
admin.mgLawfulBasisUnavailable: Lawful basis per population belongs here, but is built together with populations. We show no figures until they are real.
admin.mgMemberBounced: Address does not answer — the last send bounced {when}
admin.mgMemberObjected: Has declined to take part in surveys
admin.mgMembersRemoveNote: Members are added and deactivated under Users.
admin.mgNewDesc: Add a rule to make a segment. Without a rule it becomes a fixed group.
admin.mgPopulationsUnavailable: Populations — which keep customer, employee and supplier data apart, each with its own lawful basis and retention — are not built yet. Until they are, neither groups nor segments have a population, and we show none. They arrive together with lawful basis per population.
admin.mgSegmentsDesc: Rule-based and self-updating. Change the rule and the history is marked.
admin.mgSuppressDuplicate: That address is already on the opt-out list.
admin.mgSuppressHow: Opt-outs are recorded here. An unsubscribe link in email comes later, and will add the address straight to this list.
admin.mgSuppressNote: The opt-out list overrides every send, including addresses that arrive in a synchronised group.
admin.mgSuppressScope1: It applies to every future send from the organisation — including addresses that arrive in a synchronised group later.
admin.mgSuppressScope2: It does not delete answers already given. Deletion belongs under Privacy and GDPR.
admin.mgSuppressScope3: Only an administrator can lift it, and lifting it is logged.
admin.mgSuppressedCount: {count, plural, =0 {No opt-outs} one {# opt-out} other {# opt-outs}}
admin.mgSyncUnavailable: No directory sync is connected. Members are added manually or by import.
admin.oAllowSelfServe: Let team leads create their own surveys
admin.oBrandMailDesc: Shown at the top of the invitation
admin.oRemindersDesc: Follows the schedule you set per survey
admin.oSsoBreakGlass: Can sign in without Entra ID
admin.oSsoBreakGlassDesc: At least one active administrator must always be able to sign in with a password or email link, so the organisation can get back in if the directory fails.
admin.orgThresholdAdminOnly: Only an administrator may change a survey’s threshold, and not even an administrator may go below {k}.
admin.orgThresholdNote: New surveys of natural persons start at {k} answers. {k} is also the organisation’s floor: an individual survey may be set higher, not lower. The threshold can never be set below two.
admin.orgThresholdOrgSurveys: Surveys addressed to organisations have no threshold — answers are attributed to the organisation by name.
admin.orgThresholdRedaktorMayLower: «Allow editors to lower the threshold» is on for the organisation: editors may change an individual survey’s threshold, and it may then be set below {k}.
admin.pAutoDeleteDesc: Free text and individual answers are removed after the retention period
admin.pConsentDesc: The respondent confirms what is stored
admin.pEuOnly: Store data only in the EU/EEA
admin.pIpLoggingDesc: Answers cannot then be traced back to a device
admin.pMinResponsesDesc: Default {k} answers for new surveys · never below 2 · statutory templates carry their own
admin.pMinResponsesLocked: Always on — enforced in the database
admin.retentionNoteMonths: Raw data is deleted after {months} months. Figures already frozen in a published report are kept.
admin.retentionNoteNever: Raw data is never deleted automatically. Figures already frozen in a published report are kept either way.
admin.roleNote: Administrators manage settings and privacy. Editors create and send surveys. Readers only see aggregated results — never individual answers.
admin.saveFailed: Could not save. Please try again.
admin.thresholdTwoAlternative: If seeing individual answers is the point, “Named” is the mode that does that without a promise it cannot keep.
admin.thresholdTwoGdpr: At a threshold of 2 the aggregate is personal data in practice. Access, rectification, erasure and retention then apply to the results, not only to the answers.
admin.thresholdTwoWarning: At a threshold of 2, whoever answers can work out what the other person answered: they know their own answer, they see the average, and they subtract. That is not weakened anonymity — it is disclosure by arithmetic.

splash.heroBadge: Norwegian and English · data in Norway and the EEA
splash.heroLine2: And you know what to do next.
splash.heroBody: Most surveys die in two places: nobody bothers to answer, and the answers end up in a spreadsheet nobody opens. HeiTuva removes both. Five minutes to build, 90 seconds to answer, a finished report for your leadership team the same day.
splash.proof1Label: answer when we ask by SMS — average across pilot customers
splash.proof2Label: is all it takes to answer
splash.proof3Label: with a ready template, deadline and report
splash.showTitle: From question to heat map to report — no spreadsheets
splash.showBody: The heat map puts every team against every question. Red is where you need to step in. Teams below the organisation's threshold are hidden automatically, and one click lifts the chart into your report.
splash.drivers1Desc: Built for the phone, no login, with the time stated before the first question. People answer because it is easier than skipping it.
splash.drivers2Desc: Nobody can see who said what — not even an administrator. Below the threshold, no numbers are shown at all.
splash.drivers3Title: You show what came of it
splash.drivers3Desc: “You asked for fewer meetings — Thursdays are now meeting-free.” Nothing lifts the next round as much.
splash.useTitle: What people actually use HeiTuva for
splash.useBody: Every template is ready to send. Change what you like, reuse wording that has been tested before, and save your own questions so the next colleague does not have to invent them again.
splash.useCases1Desc: Three to five fixed questions that show which way things are going, before anything grows.
splash.useCases2Desc: The big round, compared with last year and broken down per team.
splash.useCases3Desc: Ask new people while the impression is fresh. Sends itself after the start date.
splash.useCases4Desc: Put the QR code on the screen in the room and get answers before people head home.
splash.useCases5Desc: Ask customers right after delivery: would they recommend you, and what could have been better.
splash.useCases6Desc: One question, one link, answers within the hour. Works just as well for friends.
splash.legalTitle: Working environment, equality and supply-chain duties — documented as you go
splash.legalBody: Every duty has its template, checklist, deadline and owner. The report writes itself with method, participation, findings and actions — and is archived with a signature, so last year's version always sits right beside it.
splash.stepTitle: Four steps from question to change
splash.steps1Desc: Follow the wizard or pick a template. We flag it if a question is leading or is really two questions.
splash.steps2Desc: Pull recipients from CSV, Excel, Entra ID or Google. Send by email, SMS, link or QR.
splash.steps3Desc: All rounds in one view, a heat map per team, and the themes people write about most.
splash.steps4Desc: A report for your leadership team in one click. Tell people what you did — that is why they answer next time.
splash.priceTitle: Start free. Pay when it is worth it.
splash.priceFine: All plans: data in the EU/EEA, a data processing agreement, no numbers below the organisation's threshold, and support in Nordic languages and English. Prices excl. VAT.
splash.plans1Desc: For one team, or one question you simply need answered.
splash.plans2Desc: For teams that ask regularly and report upwards.
splash.plans2Features2: Shared overview and heat map per team
splash.plans2Features3: Report templates, sharing by role and scheduled sends
splash.plans2Features5: CSV, Excel, Entra ID and Google
splash.plans2Features6: A shared question bank for the whole company
splash.plans3Desc: For organisations with legal duties, several units and auditors at the door.
splash.plans3Features2: Compliance reports with archive and signing
splash.plans3Features3: SSO login, roles and a full audit log
splash.plans3Features5: A dedicated adviser to get you started
splash.faq1A: Yes. We store no link between person and answer, and show no numbers below the threshold. If a team is below the threshold, not even an administrator sees it broken down.
splash.faq2A: On servers in Oslo and Frankfurt. The data processing agreement, privacy notice and risk assessment are ready in Admin, and raw data is deleted automatically after the retention period you choose.
splash.faq3Q: Do people need to log in or install anything?
splash.faq3A: No. A link, QR code or SMS opens the survey straight on their phone. One question at a time, around 90 seconds.
splash.faq4Q: Can we ask in several languages?
splash.faq4A: Yes. A survey can go out in Norwegian, Swedish, Danish and English at once — each person answers in their own language, and the answers land in the same report.
splash.faq5A: You pick a plan, or continue on the free tier. Nothing is deleted unless you ask us to.
splash.endTitle: Could you have a survey out before lunch?
splash.endBody: Free for 30 days, no card. Import recipients from CSV or Entra ID and send today.

legal.draftNotice: DRAFT — this text has not yet been reviewed by a lawyer and does not apply as an agreement until it has.
legal.privacy1P: HeiTuva is provided by Nordisk Studio AS, Storgata 12, 0155 Oslo, Norway. For organisations that use HeiTuva to ask their employees, the organisation is the controller and Nordisk Studio AS is the processor. This notice explains what we do with data in both roles.
legal.privacy2H: What we process about you as someone who administers HeiTuva
legal.privacy2P:
When you create an account we store your name, work email, your organisation's name and your role. We also keep a log of actions that change settings, roles and privacy choices (the audit log), so the organisation can document who did what. We do not store IP addresses or browser information tied to you.

The basis is the agreement with your organisation (GDPR art. 6(1)(b)) and our legitimate interest in securing the service (art. 6(1)(f)).
legal.privacy3H: What we process about you as someone answering a survey
legal.privacy3P:
When you answer anonymously the answer is stored without any link to you: no invitation ID, no user, no IP address, and the time is rounded to the hour. The database has a technical constraint that prevents an anonymous answer from ever being tied to a person. The organisation sees results only once enough people in the same group have answered — never below the organisation's threshold, which is never lower than two — and free text is never shown together with a group below that threshold.

When a survey is set to “with name”, you see that clearly before answering, and your answer is stored with your name. Your invitation link is personal and stored only as a hash; it cannot be reconstructed from the database.

Surveys addressed to organisations — supplier due diligence under the Transparency Act, for example — are a different case: you answer on behalf of the organisation, the answer is attributed to it by name, and no threshold applies. The survey says so before you answer.
legal.privacy4P: All data is stored in the EU/EEA: the database with Supabase in Frankfurt (eu-central-1), the application with Vercel in EU regions, email via Amazon SES in Stockholm (eu-north-1), SMS via LINK Mobility (Nordics), error reporting via Sentry in the EU. No personal data is transferred outside the EEA.
legal.privacy5P: Answers are deleted after the organisation's chosen retention period (24 months by default) by an automatic job. Account data is deleted when the organisation ends the agreement, after a 30-day grace period. The audit log is kept for the life of the agreement, because it is the organisation's documentation.
legal.privacy6P:
You have the right of access, rectification, erasure and data portability, and to object to processing based on legitimate interest. For data your organisation processes about you, contact the organisation; we help them answer within the deadlines. For data we process as controller, contact personvern@heituva.no. You may complain to Datatilsynet.

Anonymous answers cannot be found for you — that is the whole point of their being anonymous.
legal.privacy7P: Supabase (database, sign-in, storage — Frankfurt), Vercel (hosting — EU), Amazon Web Services (email — Stockholm), LINK Mobility (SMS — Norway), Cloudflare (bot protection on the front page), Sentry (error reporting — EU). The full list with purposes is in the data processing agreement.
legal.privacy8P: Nordisk Studio AS, Storgata 12, 0155 Oslo, Norway. personvern@heituva.no.
legal.dpa1P: This agreement is between the organisation using HeiTuva (the controller) and Nordisk Studio AS (the processor), and covers all processing the processor carries out on the controller's behalf in HeiTuva. The purpose is running employee surveys and the statutory documentation under the Working Environment Act, the Transparency Act and the Equality and Anti-Discrimination Act.
legal.dpa2H: Nature of the processing and categories
legal.dpa2P: Categories of data subjects: employees and others the organisation invites. Categories of data: name, email, mobile number, group membership, survey answers (anonymous or named at the organisation's choice), and free text. Special categories may occur in free text; the processor handles them only as part of the answer and not for its own purposes.
legal.dpa3P: The processor processes data only on documented instructions from the controller. The settings in HeiTuva (anonymity, retention, who has access) are such instructions. The processor notifies without delay if, in its view, an instruction infringes data protection law.
legal.dpa4P: Persons processing data at the processor are bound by confidentiality. Technical measures include: row-level security in the database separating organisations from one another; a threshold before any result is shown for a group of natural persons, enforced in the database — the organisation's own threshold, never lower than two; no threshold applies to surveys addressed to organisations, where the answer is attributed to the organisation by name; anonymous answers stored without any link to a person, enforced by a database constraint; invitation links stored only as hashes; encryption in transit and at rest; an append-only audit log; daily backups with point-in-time recovery.
legal.dpa5P: The controller gives general authorisation for the sub-processors listed in the privacy notice: Supabase Inc. (database, sign-in, storage — Frankfurt, EU), Vercel Inc. (application hosting — EU regions), Amazon Web Services EMEA SARL (email delivery — Stockholm), LINK Mobility AS (SMS — Oslo), Cloudflare Inc. (bot protection on the front page, no answer data), Functional Software Inc. / Sentry (error reporting — EU, without free text). The processor gives 30 days' notice of new sub-processors; the controller may object within that period.
legal.dpa6P: Data is stored and processed in the EU/EEA. No transfer to third countries takes place as part of the service.
legal.dpa7P: The processor assists the controller in meeting data subjects' rights (access, rectification, erasure, portability) through the tools under Administration → Privacy and GDPR, and on request. In the event of a personal data breach the processor notifies the controller without undue delay and at the latest within 24 hours of becoming aware, with the information article 33(3) requires, in phases if necessary.
legal.dpa8P: The controller may request documentation of compliance and may, once a year with 30 days' notice, carry out or commission an independent audit.
legal.dpa9P: This agreement runs for the life of the customer agreement. On termination all personal data is deleted no later than 30 days after the controller has exported it, unless law requires longer retention. A signed version of this agreement with the organisation's name and date is issued at contract and is available under Administration → Privacy and GDPR → Documentation.

usecases.title: Use cases
usecases.lead: Nine surveys people actually run. Each with the setup, the question types and the report that goes with it.
usecases.report: What you get in the report
usecases.noPack: The template for this one is not finished yet. The setup below describes how it will look.
usecases.pulsIntro: Three to five fixed questions that show the direction early. A pulse survey is the simplest route to a high response rate, and it gives you history between the big rounds.
usecases.pulsWhy1: You see changes before they become personnel cases.
usecases.pulsWhy2: Short rounds keep the response rate high over time.
usecases.pulsWhy3: The trend line documents your health-and-safety work between the annual rounds.
usecases.pulsTypes: Scale 1–5 · Smileys · Free text · Yes / no
usecases.pulsEx1: How has your week at work been?
usecases.pulsEx2: I have what I need to do my job well
usecases.pulsEx3: What would make next week better?
usecases.pulsReport1: Trend per week and per team
usecases.pulsAnonNote: Anonymous by default. A team below the threshold gets no column of its own.
usecases.pulsTipBody: Five questions is enough. Add more and the response rate drops noticeably.
usecases.medarbeiderIntro: The big round, measuring engagement, leadership, role clarity and belonging. Results are compared with last year and broken down per unit.
usecases.medarbeiderWhy1: Gives a whole picture of the working environment, not just this week’s mood.
usecases.medarbeiderWhy2: Comparison with last year shows whether the measures worked.
usecases.medarbeiderWhy3: Documents systematic health-and-safety work under the Working Environment Act § 3-1.
usecases.medarbeiderTypes: Matrix · Scale 1–5 · Multiple choice · Free text
usecases.medarbeiderEx1: I would recommend this workplace to a friend
usecases.medarbeiderEx2: My manager gives me useful feedback
usecases.medarbeiderReport4: Action plan with an owner and a deadline
usecases.medarbeiderAnonNote: Anonymous. Units below the threshold are not shown in the report — if only one is hidden, the second-smallest is hidden too.
usecases.medarbeiderTipBody: A round with no visible follow-up costs you the next one’s response rate.
usecases.psykososialIntro: The Working Environment Act requires you to map psychosocial risk, document the findings and follow them up. The template covers demands, control, leadership, harassment, health and organisation.
usecases.psykososialWhy1: The statutory mapping, with the documentation the inspection asks for.
usecases.psykososialWhy2: Risk per topic area, not one overall score.
usecases.psykososialWhy3: Findings become tasks with an owner, a deadline and a legal basis.
usecases.psykososialTypes: Scale 1–5 · Yes / no · Free text · «Don’t know» option
usecases.psykososialEx1: I can report censurable conditions without fearing the consequences
usecases.psykososialEx2: How often do you have so much to do that you cannot finish your tasks?
usecases.psykososialEx3: Do you get help and support from your immediate manager?
usecases.psykososialReport2: Groups too small to get their own results, with the legal basis
usecases.psykososialReport3: Action plan with an owner and a deadline
usecases.psykososialReport4: Signature fields for the safety representative and the committee
usecases.psykososialAnonNote: Always anonymous. «Don’t know» is its own option, so nobody has to guess.
usecases.psykososialTipBody: The safety representative and the committee must be involved before you send, not shown the report afterwards. They are not a separate role in HeiTuva — they sign the statutory report.
usecases.trakasseringIntro: Maps bullying, harassment, discrimination and whether people dare to speak up. The topic needs stricter anonymity than an ordinary survey.
usecases.trakasseringSetupV4: The channel is shown in the form
usecases.trakasseringWhy1: The duty to prevent and to look into it is yours whether or not anyone has reported.
usecases.trakasseringWhy2: A speak-up climate is measurable, and it is what decides whether you hear about things.
usecases.trakasseringWhy3: An anonymous mapping surfaces what would otherwise first appear as a personnel case.
usecases.trakasseringTypes: Yes / no · Multiple choice · Scale 1–5 · Free text
usecases.trakasseringEx1: In the past twelve months, have you experienced bullying or exclusion at work?
usecases.trakasseringEx2: Do you know where to report if something serious happens?
usecases.trakasseringEx3: Are you afraid of negative consequences if you report?
usecases.trakasseringReport2: Speak-up climate and awareness of the procedure
usecases.trakasseringReport3: Findings that trigger the duty to investigate
usecases.trakasseringReport4: Measures and an updated whistleblowing procedure
usecases.trakasseringAnonNote: Stricter anonymity: the template locks the threshold at eight, and no group is shown with fewer answers. Quotes in a report are chosen by a person, never automatically.
usecases.trakasseringTipBody: Do not bolt harassment questions onto an ordinary engagement survey. The topic needs its own round and its own threshold.
usecases.likestillingIntro: The activity and reporting duty requires you to examine discrimination risk, map pay gaps and involuntary part-time work, and report the findings publicly.
usecases.likestillingSetupV3: Anonymous, broken down by the groups you have
usecases.likestillingWhy1: The activity duty requires the mapping, and the reporting duty requires it published.
usecases.likestillingWhy2: Involuntary part-time is a number you have to know before you can do anything about it.
usecases.likestillingWhy3: The report is the documentation, and it is written from the answers.
usecases.likestillingTypes: Multiple choice · Number · Scale 1–5 · Free text
usecases.likestillingEx1: Do you work part-time, and is that your own wish?
usecases.likestillingEx2: What contracted hours would you like?
usecases.likestillingEx3: Do you experience equal opportunities in internal recruitment?
usecases.likestillingReport4: A draft of the public statement
usecases.likestillingAnonNote: Anonymous. A group is shown only when it is above the threshold. Gender is not a field HeiTuva stores — the breakdown follows the groups you have.
usecases.likestillingTipBody: Self-reported pay is not enough for the reporting duty. Pull the figures aggregated per job group from your payroll system — the integration is not switched on yet, so for now you do that outside HeiTuva.
usecases.aktsomhetIntro: A form to your suppliers about working conditions, human rights and sub-suppliers. The answers are the basis for the statement due by 30 June.
usecases.aktsomhetWhy1: The Transparency Act requires due diligence through the whole supply chain.
usecases.aktsomhetWhy2: Answers are attributed, so the statement can name what was asked and who answered.
usecases.aktsomhetWhy3: A supplier who does not answer is itself a finding.
usecases.aktsomhetTypes: Yes / no · Multiple choice · Free text · File upload
usecases.aktsomhetEx1: Do you have written procedures prohibiting child labour at your own sub-suppliers?
usecases.aktsomhetEx2: Do employees have the right to organise?
usecases.aktsomhetEx3: Describe the findings and where in the chain they arose.
usecases.aktsomhetReport3: Measures with an owner and a deadline
usecases.aktsomhetReport4: A statement following the OECD model
usecases.aktsomhetAnonNote: Not anonymous. Answers are attributed to the company and its contact, with a traceable history.
usecases.aktsomhetTipBody: Map the suppliers with the highest risk first. The statement must show the priority, not cover everyone equally.
usecases.onboardingIntro: Sent a while after someone starts, catching what was unclear while the impression is fresh. The single strongest measure against early turnover.
usecases.onboardingSetupV1: A scheduled send after the start
usecases.onboardingWhy1: Most early turnover is decided in the first thirty days.
usecases.onboardingWhy2: What was unclear is easy to fix and easy to forget.
usecases.onboardingWhy3: The answers say more about your onboarding than about the person.
usecases.onboardingEx1: The first month matched my expectations
usecases.onboardingEx2: Did you have a buddy in your first week?
usecases.onboardingEx3: What was confusing in the first few weeks?
usecases.onboardingAnonNote: Anonymous, aggregated per cohort. A new starter must not be identifiable by their start date.
usecases.onboardingTipBody: Set the recurrence up once. A manual send is the one that gets forgotten.
usecases.kundeIntro: Ask right after a purchase, a delivery or a case. One reference figure over time, with free text explaining why it moves.
usecases.kundeSetupV1: After delivery or a closed case
usecases.kundeWhy1: One figure over time is worth more than a long survey once a year.
usecases.kundeWhy2: The free text is what tells you why the figure moved.
usecases.kundeWhy3: Asking close to the event gets you an answer people remember.
usecases.kundeTypes: NPS 0–10 · Scale 1–5 · Multiple choice · Free text
usecases.kundeEx1: How likely are you to recommend us?
usecases.kundeEx2: How did you find the delivery?
usecases.kundeEx3: What could we have done better?
usecases.kundeReport1: NPS over time and per channel
usecases.kundeAnonNote: Anonymous unless the customer asks to be contacted. Then the answer is attributed, and it says so before they answer.
usecases.kundeTipBody: A score plus a free-text «why» beats a long form nobody finishes.
usecases.exitIntro: A short form on the last working day. Answers are aggregated over the year and show why people actually leave, rather than what they say in the exit interview.
usecases.exitWhy1: People are more honest in writing than in a conversation with their manager.
usecases.exitWhy2: The pattern across a year is the finding; one answer is not.
usecases.exitWhy3: Turnover has causes you can act on, and most of them are known before people leave.
usecases.exitEx1: What was the most important reason you left?
usecases.exitEx3: What should we have changed to keep you?
usecases.exitReport1: Reasons for leaving across the year
usecases.exitAnonNote: Anonymous and aggregated. Individual answers are never shown, however few people leave.
usecases.exitTipBody: A single exit answer is an anecdote. The year’s answers together are a finding.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.unavailableHint: This integration has not been built yet.
integrations.detailProtocol: Microsoft Graph — HeiTuva reads from the directory
integrations.detailNote: HeiTuva fetches users from Entra ID on a schedule. New accounts become members, department becomes group, and accounts deactivated in the directory stop receiving surveys. HeiTuva never writes back to the directory.
integrations.detailFieldsPromise: Nothing beyond this is read from the directory.
integrations.detailRefusal_not_built: Not read. The columns exist, but HeiTuva does not yet accept groups from the directory.
integrations.detailRefusal_self_entered: Not read. A job title is what each person writes about herself on Profil, and the directory must not overwrite that.
integrations.detailRefusal_not_a_trigger: Not read. A field in the directory describes a person; it does not decide what the product does to her.
integrations.detailScopesNote: Read only, and one direction only. HeiTuva never writes back to the directory, and holds no access that could.
integrations.detailStepDesc_scope: You decide which users are in scope, in Entra.
integrations.detailLogNoHistory: HeiTuva stores the outcome of the last call, not a history. A log of who arrived and who left is personal data about staff, and needs a purpose and a retention period first.
integrations.detailLogFailing: {count, plural, one {# consecutive call has failed} other {# consecutive calls have failed}}
integrations.detailScopeUsers: Read users: name, email, department and whether the account is active
integrations.detailScopesPlanned: This is the permission your administrator will be asked to approve. We do not ask for more than we use.
integrations.detailGroupsAreDepartments: The groups below come from the «department» field in the directory. One person belongs to one department, which is why department is what results are broken down by.
integrations.detailGroupsNotEntra: The groups you have in Entra are not fetched. They overlap, so one person would count in two cells — and a group with no single leader has nobody who owns the number. They belong as recipient lists, not as a breakdown.
integrations.detailDepartmentCoverage: {with} of {seen} got a department. {without} are missing, and they are placed in no group.
integrations.connectPending: Connecting requires HeiTuva to be registered in Entra. Coming.
integrations.connectionHeld: Connected to the directory {tenant}. The key is encrypted at our end and is shown nowhere — not here either.
integrations.detailStepDesc_consent: An administrator in Entra approves HeiTuva reading users. Once.
integrations.detailStepDesc_first: Runs straight after approval. A few minutes for most.
integrations.detailStepDesc_schedule: Every night. If something fails the screen says so — it does not sit there looking successful.
